finding_3_one_sided_vertical_rectifier.code: spatial/safety.py ReferenceSpatialSupervisor.action: `if safety.inhibited and applied[2] < 0: applied[2] = min(limits[2], downward/delay)`; two_axis/safety.py:180 is the same law.
finding_3_one_sided_vertical_rectifier.mechanism: A descending vehicle is braked with up to full upward authority; an ascending one passes through untouched. The direct-acceleration plant has no restoring force on altitude, so zero-mean exploration integrates upward. `inhibited` is set by track_not_trustworthy on 56-60 % of a fresh policy's steps and by vertical_stopping_margin on 7-10 %, so it is active at every altitude.
finding_3_one_sided_vertical_rectifier.measured_2d_on_the_PRIMARY_reference_con: two_axis_reference_v28_active, fresh policy, 40 episodes at difficulty 1.0: the descent_brake fires on 34 % of steps and turns a requested -0.169 m/s^2 into an applied -0.013, i.e. 92 % of the commanded descent removed. Median climb +1.75 m, 8/40 SAFETY_ENVELOPE_VIOLATION, 31/40 SAFE_ABORT. The planar episode starts at 6.2 m and has no 20 m ceiling, so the same law shows up as hovering rather than as a runaway.
finding_3_one_sided_vertical_rectifier.why_the_oracle_never_saw_it: the swept PD sits inside the terminal-descent corridor on 64 % of its steps and has only 2.8 % of its actions overridden.

finding_4_ppo_regresses_on_actions_that_.code: two_axis/learning.py records safety_flags['intervened'] on every Transition; neither PPOTrainer.update nor ppo_minibatch_update reads it. Both regress on raw_command.

finding_5_single_episode_rollouts.detail: the spatial runs use episodes_per_iteration=1 (~110-130 decisions) with advantage_normalization='rollout', so every advantage is centred inside its own episode and no cross-episode comparison survives. The 2D route uses decisions_per_iteration=2048.
finding_5_single_episode_rollouts.THIS_IS_THE_DOMINANT_ONE: the nine controlled cells below rank the three repairs and only this one moves PPO. Every cell that batches 12 complete episodes per update converges to TASK_TIMEOUT (C 0.833, D 0.542, H 0.250), i.e. the policy finally follows the terminal ordering TASK_TIMEOUT -12 > SAFE_ABORT -15. Every cell that keeps one episode per update stays trapped in SAFE_ABORT at 0.75-0.96.
finding_5_single_episode_rollouts.budget_is_not_the_constraint: cell I ran 7200 episodes -- three times the others -- with one episode per update and the symmetric hold. Result: 6073/7200 SAFE_ABORT and exactly ONE TASK_TIMEOUT in 7200 episodes, held-out return -16.1. Cell C used a third of that budget with 12-episode batches and reached -10.5 with zero unsafe outcomes. The constraint is the batch, not the wall-clock.
finding_5_single_episode_rollouts.best_cell: C_batched: held-out unsafe 0.000, abort 0.167, TASK_TIMEOUT 0.833, mean return -10.5 against the baseline's -22.4, and the only cell that produced SUCCESS during training at all (2 episodes, one of them inside the last 400).

finding_7_the_arms_can_represent_the_sol.claim: Supervised imitation of the swept controller lands, so neither the observation nor the architecture is the obstacle. The whole gap is exploration and credit assignment.
finding_7_the_arms_can_represent_the_sol.method: 120 teacher episodes (40 seeds x difficulty 0.0/0.5/1.0) from the swept causal controller, loss in ACTION space (mean((tanh(mu) - a_teacher)^2)), then DAgger rounds that relabel the learner's own states. Actor only; no reward, no PPO. Held out on seeds 3001-3024, deterministic.
finding_7_the_arms_can_represent_the_sol.harness_note: an earlier version regressed mu onto atanh(clip(a, +-0.999)); the teacher saturates often, so those targets went to +-3.8 and the objective was dominated by the clipping constant. Numbers from that version are not comparable.

training_failure_diagnosis_20261005.conclusion: The task, the reward, the oracle ceiling, the ontology's observability and the arms' representational capacity are all cleared. What is left is that the supervisor prevents the policy from ever executing a descent, and that PPO is then told the policy asked for the descent the supervisor removed.

what_the_cells_rank.dominant: complete-episode batches. Only the batched cells escape SAFE_ABORT; see finding_5.
what_the_cells_rank.neutral_to_harmful_for_learning: the symmetric vertical hold. Alone it is barely distinguishable from the baseline (E -20.2 against A -22.4) and on top of batches it COSTS performance (C -10.5 -> H -16.1, TASK_TIMEOUT 0.833 -> 0.250). What it does buy is safety: last-400 envelope deaths 139 -> 44 and a 19.71 m -> 0.70 m median climb at the easy rung.
what_the_cells_rank.no_measurable_benefit: the executed-action mask. B improves on A, but C (batch alone) beats D (batch + mask) on return (-10.5 vs -12.3) and on unsafe (0.000 vs 0.042). Its binary shape is also actively wrong once the hold is in place: executed fraction 0.046 in G and 0.077 in F against 0.298 for the mask alone.
what_the_cells_rank.none_of_them_lands: every cell reports 0 SUCCESS on the easy rung across 1590-4800 easy episodes, and held-out landing is 0.000 everywhere except D's single episode in 24. They converge to holding station to the deadline and never enter the descent corridor. The only route to a landing policy measured today is supervised imitation (finding_7).
what_the_cells_rank.correction: an earlier version of this record led with the vertical ratchet as the fix. The nine-cell ranking does not support that: the ratchet is a real defect with a real safety effect, but the single-episode rollout is what was stopping PPO.
